title: Notes and observations from #49ers practice No. 13, a long one that was the last one of this camp open for fans: - Three new additions to the list of players not participating today: G Dominick Puni (concussion), WR Demarcus Robinson (undisclosed) and DT Gracen Halton (ankle). - The Niners also had a few injury scares during practice. DT C.J. West and DE Titus Leo were hurt on separate plays that happened within minutes of each other. Both needed help getting up and then slowly made their way to the locker room for further evaluation. They did not finish the session. - WRs Deebo Samuel and Jacob Cowing were also shaken up but both returned and finished practice. Cowing made a highlight-reel catch after he came back which we'll get to in a minute. And Samuel was all over the place today. - Here's the full list of non participants on Sunday: Puni, Halton, Robinson, RB Christian McCaffrey (tightness), LB Luke Gifford (hamstring), DE Nick Bosa (soreness/tendinitis), FB Kyle Juszczyk (broken finger), OL Brett Toth (concussion), QB Kurtis Rourke (undisclosed/ribs), WR Christian Kirk (calf), S Malik Mustapha (hamstring), RB Kaelon Black (adductor), RB Jordan James (rib), DL Keion White (adductor), OT Vederian Lowe (ankle), CB Nate Hobbs (groin) Players on PUP: TE George Kittle (achilles), RB Isaac Guerendo (pec), DL Mykel Williams (ACL) - Perhaps most notable here: We had our first side field Bosa sighting since he began experiencing tendinitis and soreness early in camp. He did an extensive workout on the side field. A (public) step in the right direction for him. - Rourke didn't practice again and though his specific injury has not been disclosed, OC Klay Kubiak said he doesn't think it will be long before Rourke returns. - WR KhaDarel Hodge was back in pads and uniform after missing on Saturday. - Observations from 1v1 pass rush drills: Gotta start with the rookie, Enrique Cruz Jr. Anyone who has read this space has probably noticed how it's been mentioned that he's struggled often here. So it's only fair we start with praise for what was easily his best performance in these drills in this camp. I wrote "best rep of camp?" after he showed quick feet and second reaction ability against Ogbo Okoronkwo for a win in one rep and then he topped it with his showing on the last rep of this drill against DE Xavier Thomas. Baby steps but at least signs of progress and it's worth noting his fellow line mates were invested, cheering loudly for him for his work in these today... DT Alfred Collins got involved here for the first time in this camp and flashed his power a little bit against Kion Smith after not getting much against Robert Jones... Speaking of, Jones had a handful of solid reps today. Pass pro is the question here but these were mostly more consistent and better than what we've seen... Carver Willis is still getting comfortable here but he had his share of issues trying to block Sebastian Valdez, Osa Odighizuwa and West. - Have mentioned UDFA DT James Thompson Jr. here a bunch but it's worth noting he was first up to step in for West when he was shaken up today. I had Thompson down for a couple of wins in 1v1 and then multiple run stuffs and a shared would-be sack during team drills. - A good day for QBs Brock Purdy and Mac Jones today, including a good amount of completions on deep balls. I had Purdy at 12-of-17 (didn't count a few plays for either penalties or would-be sacks) with Jones at 17-of-20. Purdy dropped in a beautiful deep ball to Malik Turner, who was well covered but made a nice over the shoulder grab for a huge gain. He later connected with Cowing, who was shaken up on a deep pass broken up by Marques Sigle, but returned to dive and haul one in over his shoulder for a big gain. Purdy also hit WR Mike Evans for a big gain, Deebo on a crosser for a chunk and found WR De'Zhaun Stribling on a crosser for a touchdown in the red zone... Jones had a really strong red zone period, throwing touchdowns to Will Pauling and Wesley Grimes and hitting Turner for a deep score outside of the red zone as well. He and Stribling also connected on a deep ball after a well-schemed play had Stribling running man-to-man against LB Larry Wirth. Jones has settled in and looked more like the guy we saw in last year's camp over the past few days. - Nice day for Turner, who has been a practice squad mainstay over the past few years. He made multiple catches deep and is still getting plenty of run in key special teams roles. Wonder how the math works for him to earn a roster spot but he's been a nice option for them shuttling between practice squad and active roster in the past. - Deebo was very involved today and made a handful of plays regardless of who was at QB. He's getting the ball in all kinds of ways. Seemed like maybe he got a stinger after a catch down the left sideline near the end zone but he shook it off (amidst the chuckles of LT Trent Williams) and finished the session. - Frustrating sequence for CB Renardo Green (who has had a nice camp) in the red zone against Evans. He got flagged for DPI on a deep ball for Evans (was a close one but seemed he impeded Evans by grabbing his left arm) then got a (more questionable IMO) holding call. After he defended a throw for Evans in the end zone that fell incomplete, he turned to the official and offered surprise that he didn't get a hat trick of flags. - Some defensive highlights: Stout was in coverage on the deep completion to Turner and it was just a good throw/better catch scenario but he bounced back with sticky coverage on Stribling to force an incompletion to close practice... Lenoir continues to be all over it in coverage... Jack Jones had a PBU on a throw from Jones... Jaden Dugger did a nice job disengaging from a block to make a run stop... Thompson and Sam Okuayinonu broke through for a would-be shared sack... Sigle had the nice pass break up on a deep ball for Cowing. Was also slow to get up up but he was OK... S Ashtyn Davis tipped a pass from Jones that LB Tatum Bethune nearly picked off. - Got to see some various kick and punt returner combinations today. My sense is the Niners would love Jordan Watkins to take a step forward and potentially handle punts. But he muffed one today and was visibly upset about it afterward. Cowing, Will Pauling and even Jack Jones got some opportunities. Hadn't noticed Jones doing it before but he looked pretty comfortable back there... Among the kick return combos (these will rotate and change a lot, of course): Deebo and Cowing/Watkins and Sincere McCormick/Khalil Herbert and Pauling. - That'll do it for this one. Programming notes: I'll be in LA for joint practice with Chargers on Tuesday. From there, Niners don't have many more open practices. These notes will continue in some format but will be tweaked as there are some rule changes in what can be reported from the field and not as season nears. As always, thanks for reading and enjoy your Sunday.

Speaking of, Jones had a handful of solid reps today. Pass pro is the question here but these were mostly more consistent and better than what we've seen... Carver Willis is still getting comfortable here but he had his share of issues trying to block Sebastian Valdez, Osa Odighizuwa and West. 

- Have mentioned UDFA DT James Thompson Jr. here a bunch but it's worth noting he was first up to step in for West when he was shaken up today. I had Thompson down for a couple of wins in 1v1 and then multiple run stuffs and a shared would-be sack during team drills. 

- A good day for QBs Brock Purdy and Mac Jones today, including a good amount of completions on deep balls. I had Purdy at 12-of-17 (didn't count a few plays for either penalties or would-be sacks) with Jones at 17-of-20. Purdy dropped in a beautiful deep ball to Malik Turner, who was well covered but made a nice over the shoulder grab for a huge gain. He later connected with Cowing, who was shaken up on a deep pass broken up by Marques Sigle, but returned to dive and haul one in over his shoulder for a big gain. Purdy also hit WR Mike Evans for a big gain, Deebo on a crosser for a chunk and found WR De'Zhaun Stribling on a crosser for a touchdown in the red zone... Jones had a really strong red zone period, throwing touchdowns to Will Pauling and Wesley Grimes and hitting Turner for a deep score outside of the red zone as well. He and Stribling also connected on a deep ball after a well-schemed play had Stribling running man-to-man against LB Larry Wirth. Jones has settled in and looked more like the guy we saw in last year's camp over the past few days. 

- Nice day for Turner, who has been a practice squad mainstay over the past few years. He made multiple catches deep and is still getting plenty of run in key special teams roles. Wonder how the math works for him to earn a roster spot but he's been a nice option for them shuttling between practice squad and active roster in the past.

- Deebo was very involved today and made a handful of plays regardless of who was at QB. He's getting the ball in all kinds of ways. Seemed like maybe he got a stinger after a catch down the left sideline near the end zone but he shook it off (amidst the chuckles of LT Trent Williams) and finished the session. 

- Frustrating sequence for CB Renardo Green (who has had a nice camp) in the red zone against Evans. He got flagged for DPI on a deep ball for Evans (was a close one but seemed he impeded Evans by grabbing his left arm) then got a (more questionable IMO) holding call. After he defended a throw for Evans in the end zone that fell incomplete, he turned to the official and offered surprise that he didn't get a hat trick of flags. 

- Some defensive highlights: Stout was in coverage on the deep completion to Turner and it was just a good throw/better catch scenario but he bounced back with sticky coverage on Stribling to force an incompletion to close practice... Lenoir continues to be all over it in coverage... Jack Jones had a PBU on a throw from Jones... Jaden Dugger did a nice job disengaging from a block to make a run stop... Thompson and Sam Okuayinonu broke through for a would-be shared sack... Sigle had the nice pass break up on a deep ball for Cowing. Was also slow to get up up but he was OK... S Ashtyn Davis tipped a pass from Jones that LB Tatum Bethune nearly picked off.

- Got to see some various kick and punt returner combinations today. My sense is the Niners would love Jordan Watkins to take a step forward and potentially handle punts. But he muffed one today and was visibly upset about it afterward. Cowing, Will Pauling and even Jack Jones got some opportunities. Hadn't noticed Jones doing it before but he looked pretty comfortable back there... Among the kick return combos (these will rotate and change a lot, of course): Deebo and Cowing/Watkins and Sincere McCormick/Khalil Herbert and Pauling. 

- That'll do it for this one. Programming notes: I'll be in LA for joint practice with Chargers on Tuesday. From there, Niners don't have many more open practices. These notes will continue in some format but will be tweaked as there are some rule changes in what can be reported from the field and not as season nears. As always, thanks for reading and enjoy your Sunday.

title: Day 14 notes - Kayode Awosika and Jake Slaughter rotated at left guard. Thought Awosika had the better day today. - Tyler Biadasz looked good again today in pass and run blocking. After a block on Teair Tart, Tart pushed him, which started a small gathering of players, but no serious fight or anything. (Justin Herbert and Denzel Perryman play-fought while players were huddled.) - Tart was sent off to work with strength coach Ben Herbert. Tart was having another dominant day before that. Had him down for one sack on a pressure. - Brenen Thompson caught a deep pass from Justin Herbert, beating Donte Jackson down one sideline. The play may have been blown dead in a real game, as Tuli Tuipulotu beat Trey Pipkins. - Herbert was accurate and comfortable today. One throw to David Njoku, up and over the arms of RJ Mickens, drew praise from OC Mike McDaniel, who yelled, “F--k yeah, 10” multiple times. - Daiyan Henley had a TFL* on an Omarion Hampton run, which looked like came due to a Slaughter missed assignment. Slaughter threw his head back in dismay, and OL coach Butch Barry yelled at him not to get frustrated. - Trey Pipkins briefly worked off to the side with a trainer during 11-on-11. Branson Taylor and Logan Taylor played LT with him out. Pipkins eventually returned. -Dalevon Campbell had an up-and-down day. I had him down for three drops, but he also had a handful of catches, including a leaping grab over Eric Rogers. He’s consistently been good throughout camp. - Charlie Kolar had two drops today after having a drop yesterday. He threw his helmet in frustration after the second drop today. - Travis Burke won all four of his 1-on-1 reps, looking as comfortable as he has so far in camp. Two wins over Nadame Tucker, one over Kyle Kennard and one over Garmon Randolph. - KLS had a bunch of good catches today, including one leaping grab. - Had Khalil Mack down for at least one sack today. He blew by fullback Alec Ingold. - Marlowe Wax was also sent off to work with strength coach Ben Herbert. DC Chris O'Leary said he hit a running back in a period he wasn't supposed to. - Trey Lance had a nice touchdown pass to Oronde Gadsden - RB Amar Johnson had a deep receiving TD from Justin Herbert. Beat Junior Colson down the sideline

Day 14 notes

- Brenen Thompson caught a deep pass from Justin Herbert, beating Donte Jackson down one sideline. The play may have been blown dead in a real game, as Tuli Tuipulotu beat Trey Pipkins.

- Herbert was accurate and comfortable today. One throw to David Njoku, up and over the arms of RJ Mickens, drew praise from OC Mike McDaniel, who yelled, “F--k yeah, 10” multiple times.

- Daiyan Henley had a TFL* on an Omarion Hampton run, which looked like came due to a Slaughter missed assignment. Slaughter threw his head back in dismay, and OL coach Butch Barry yelled at him not to get frustrated.

-Dalevon Campbell had an up-and-down day. I had him down for three drops, but he also had a handful of catches, including a leaping grab over Eric Rogers. He’s consistently been good throughout camp.

- Trey Lance had a nice touchdown pass to Oronde Gadsden 

- RB Amar Johnson had a deep receiving TD from Justin Herbert. Beat Junior Colson down the sideline

- Daiyan Henley had a TFL* on an Omarion Hampton run, which looked like came due to a Slaughter missed assignment. Slaughter threw his head back in dismay, and OL coach Butch Barry yelled at him not to get frustrated.

- Trey Pipkins briefly worked off to the side with a trainer during 11-on-11. Branson Taylor and Logan Taylor played LT with him out. Pipkins eventually returned.

-Dalevon Campbell had an up-and-down day. I had him down for three drops, but he also had a handful of catches, including a leaping grab over Eric Rogers. He’s consistently been good throughout camp.

- Charlie Kolar had two drops today after having a drop yesterday. He threw his helmet in frustration after the second drop today.

- Travis Burke won all four of his 1-on-1 reps, looking as comfortable as he has so far in camp. Two wins over Nadame Tucker, one over Kyle Kennard and one over Garmon Randolph.

- KLS had a bunch of good catches today, including one leaping grab.

- Had Khalil Mack down for at least one sack today. He blew by fullback Alec Ingold.

- Marlowe Wax was also sent off to work with strength coach Ben Herbert. DC Chris O'Leary said he hit a running back in a period he wasn't supposed to.

- Trey Lance had a nice touchdown pass to Oronde Gadsden 

- RB Amar Johnson had a deep receiving TD from Justin Herbert. Beat Junior Colson down the sideline

title: I post this picture a lot because that was a beautiful fun night where I saw a lot of Texans, old and nu, many people committed to helping Houstonians and the football community at large. All the kinds of big winning. Including @TexansCommenter, hi there all y’all👋 Love welcoming badasses to Houston, making each other feel at home. It was a super kind night in ways I needed more than I knew. Very stoked to see these dudes do their thing. Best case scenario is big lead dominance, which is hard to do at the professional level but in the range of reasonable probabilities just due to defensive experience and team chemistry/development. Running backs make that extra fun. Just the thought of that makes both young and old a little insane. People will say the key to 2026 is this or that. I think it is everybody. I got this picture because obviously lovers of Texans style football are deep running back respecters, that would be a big boost along with everyone that makes a running game work well, and I am trying to take more pix to reinforce great pure memories. Very curious to see real game stuff. Walked around the tailgates last week and the enduring thing people say is how much they enjoy getting to know more about the 2026 Texans roster. A lot of remarkable people, like most teams, you can see how DeMeco minded they are. Very best of #Texans.

title: Spent a couple days with the @Eagles on my annual Glaze Across America NFL Training Camp Tour and the biggest takeaway I walked away with… the number of people at different areas of the team are raving about how much effort @JalenHurts has put in to improving in many areas on and off the field. Can’t tell you how many “I’m really proud of him” I got. Last year he was at the center of issues but they are speaking a MUCH different tune on him so far in camp. Even guys who were previously frustrated with him were absolutely praising him for the work he’s put in and the concerted effort he has made. Good for him! It’s never too late and in this league you always need to find ways to improve, evolve and improve some more. It never ends if you want to be THAT GUY! Plus, they think this offense will be much better suited to him, the offensive line, Saquon, all around. @NFLonFOX #eagles #nfl #philadelphia
